subject: Axios: Trump has struck diesel deal with Putin because of Ukraine's refusal to halt refinery strikes
posts:
Trump cuts a Russian diesel deal with Putin after Ukraine refuses to halt oil refinery strikes.
Evidence: Axios reports, White House envoys, Miami talks. 🌐
#Aletheia #Geopolitics

Trump's team claimed the diesel deal was necessary because Ukrainian refinery strikes raised US gas prices, ignoring equivalent Russian destruction of Ukraine's grid.
Stated Judgement: (+0.2, -0.1) — Lesser Evil

In reality, the White House cut a backroom energy deal with Putin for political convenience, undercutting Ukraine's defensive leverage over high gas prices.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
A backroom deal with Moscow rewards aggression and sacrifices ally security for domestic political optics.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 24.8, z: 2)

- US Diplomacy: FAIL (-0.85, -0.90) — Rewards Russian aggression.
- Ukrainian Defense: FAIL (-0.90, -0.85) — Pressured to halt strikes.
After Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries drove up US fuel costs, Trump envoys pressured Kyiv and struck a direct fuel deal with Moscow.

The Poison:
Trading an ally's security for domestic fuel prices signals to adversaries that energy blackmail and aggression pay off.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (global energy markets) with WHO (blaming the defending victim instead of the invading aggressor).

Social Physics Analysis:
The US administration ran a Smart Selfish Maneuver: using domestic gas prices as a pretext to pressure an ally while cutting a self-serving deal with an adversary.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated economic pretexts and ally betrayal, it plots a direct trajectory toward Destruction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Domestic energy costs drive foreign policy shortcuts that abandon democratic allies.

The Unavoidable Lie: Appeasement deals stop wars.

Alethekanon:
Economic convenience cloaked as neutrality is simply moral surrender to authoritarian muscle.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks the heart to watch defenders fighting for survival get squeezed and traded away by distant power brokers seeking quick fixes.

Brothekanon:
Wild how cutting fuel deals with Putin gets spun as tough diplomacy while the folks getting bombed take the heat.

Spirithekanon:
"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil." Isaiah 5:20 PASS
Rewarding aggression while penalizing the defender corrupts justice at its root.

[Source 1 — www.pravda.com.ua] (URL: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/10/8057313/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Axios: Trump has struck diesel deal with Putin because of Ukraine's refusal to halt refinery strikes

A senior US official says Donald Trump wanted Kyiv to stop attacking Russian oil refineries unilaterally, while Ukrainian officials say his envoys threatened to cut off US intelligence sharing if the strikes continued.

Actual Article Body:
Долучайтеся до клубу УП!

US President Donald Trump has decided to strike a deal with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin to supply Russian diesel fuel to the United States because Ukraine refused to unilaterally halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Source: Axios, citing a senior US official familiar with the situation

Details: According to the official, Trump's decision came after Zelenskyy ignored half a dozen requests to stop strikes on Russian oil refineries.

Quote: "Zelenskyy told Trump and his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner that he was prepared to stop attacking Russian oil refineries if the Russians halted attacks on Ukrainian power plants.

The US official said Trump wanted Ukraine to unilaterally stop attacking Russian refineries because the strikes were contributing to high gas prices in America.

Trump didn't see the attacks on refineries as equivalent to Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid, the US official said."

Details: The official added that "the attacks on the refineries cause pain in Russia, but it causes pain for the US, too".

"Zelenskyy is misreading the room. By continuing to hit refineries, he is eroding the good will that he has built with Trump over the last six months," the official said.

According to Axios, during eight hours of talks in Miami, Trump's envoys told the Ukrainian delegation that the president would speak to Putin and lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

A Ukrainian official told Axios that Witkoff and Kushner had threatened to cut Ukraine off from US intelligence if it continued the strikes. The US official denied that any such threats had been made and said the US was a reliable partner that provided ammunition and intelligence.

In addition, Witkoff and Kushner briefed the Ukrainian delegation and European representatives on potential energy deals with Russia which the US hopes will encourage Moscow to make concessions in peace negotiations.

"Putin is hitting [Ukraine] hard but we think he is open to a discussion on ending the war. We want to work on a new proposal that will be good enough for him in order to get him to stop," the US official said.

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump reiterated his complaints on Friday about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, calling it a disgraceful and embarrassing decision that had left a stain on Norway, which hosts the Nobel committee.

Trump unleashed on Norway hours after the committee awarded this year's prize to Navi Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded Israel committed ​genocide in Gaza.

Trump called Pillay a "mystery person" during a campaign rally in Syracuse, New York. "I never heard of the person. Nobody did."

Each year of his presidency, Trump has expressed disappointment that he failed to win the prize.

"This is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision," Trump said.

He listed a number of conflicts that he claimed a role in resolving and said he has helped prevent wars from breaking out between North and South Korea, Japan and North Korea, and China and Taiwan, without providing evidence.

"The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization. And we will not forget, Norway," he said.

Actual Article Body:
This week, my wife and I are celebrating our 35th wedding anniversary. Of course, the inevitable question is, “Where would you like to go for dinner?” The ritualistic play then begins as my wife tells me she doesn’t care and asks me to choose. You can guess how the story proceeds from here. It is another example of the seeming ambiguity of choice: not necessarily knowing what we want but certainly knowing what we don’t want.

In previous essays, I’ve mentioned Jean-Paul Sartre’s Being and Nothingness, and today will be no exception. Sartre describes a man and a woman on a date. The man takes the woman’s hand. She can pull her hand away or grasp his hand firmly, with either action sending a clear signal to the man. But there is a third choice: she can do neither, leaving her hand where it is and behaving as though the situation were somehow outside her decision. That refusal to decide is itself a choice.
